extracted.intended_audience: new principal investigators (new PIs) trying to renew a first NIH R01
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based advice for new PIs preparing and evaluating the prospects of submitting a renewal (competing continuation / -06) of an initial NIH R01. Focuses on how to research prior renewals, benchmark productivity expectations, and set realistic career/funding expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding interval flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH R01 application can propose any interval of funding from 1 to 5 years (5 is most common). Some ICs will only award 4 years no matter if you try to propose 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning a renewal, explicitly choose the proposed award interval (1–5 years) but check specific IC practices because some Institutes/Centers limit awarded durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand renewal vs new application types
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI(s) can propose a followup interval which undergoes competitive review and may or may not be funded for another interval. This used to be called a competing continuation applications and now it is called a renewal application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the difference between Type 1 (new) and Type 2 (competing continuation/renewal) submissions — both are handled differently in records and in career evaluation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RePORTER to benchmark prior renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Get your butt over to RePORTER and start doing some searches. Put a 2 in the Type Code field and R01 in the mechanism field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After setting Type Code=2 and mechanism=R01, use text search keywords, your favorite Institute/Center code, or Study Section field to find closely relevant renewals. This is presented as the primary empirical method to see what renewals look like in your area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter for first-renewals (-06) and shorter awards (-05)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new PI, perhaps it might be relevant to specify -06 in the year field, to focus on first-renewals. You might want to also use -05 to pick up any shorter (or shortened) awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search the year/status codes in RePORTER to isolate first renewal attempts (-06) and detect patterns in shorter-than-usual award periods (-05) to benchmark expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare abstracts of -06 vs -01 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing the Abstracts for the -06 and -01 versions of the same project may be helpful in trying to figure out how much difference is required or permitted in the cases most similar to your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use side-by-side abstract comparisons to judge acceptable scope/aim changes between original and renewal applications within your topic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare listed publications to infer productivity expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing the Publications listed for each project may give you some clue as to productivity expectations in terms of number of pubs, journal prestige, and maybe even specificity to the topic or Aims as they appear from the Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at quantity, venues (journal prestige), and topical alignment of publications tied to funded projects to estimate what reviewers/ICs expect for renewals in your field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for survivorship bias — examine non-renewed peers
rubrics_metrics.description: Get yourself a handle on the new projects that started around the same time (give or take a few years) using the same general search criteria which did NOT result in funded renewals. Look at Productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare renewed projects to contemporaneous projects that failed to renew to identify distinguishing factors — don't infer norms only from surviving renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectation: do not rely on renewal as an easy path
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are getting the hint from all of this than banking on a renewal at the present time is a very, very bad idea… yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat renewal as uncertain and competitive; plan alternative funding strategies rather than assuming renewal will provide the next interval of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of local mentoring advice to focus solely on renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Next level is if you are getting local mentoring advice that says you should throw all your eggs in the renewal basket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify such advice empirically via RePORTER historical searches and wider benchmarking before committing career/time resources to a single renewal-focused strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine long-term historical trends in new vs renewal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Go back a fair bit in RePORTER (say 15-20 Fiscal Years) and do a similar bit of searching. You could do something like look at the ratio of new awards (Type 1) to renewals (Type 2) for a given study section or IC from back then versus now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-range Type 1 vs Type 2 ratios by study section/IC to judge whether renewals have become rarer and adjust expectations/plans accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the role of PI seniority and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: In doing a little search like this for current -06 renewals for one of my favorite ICs I Noticed Something. All of them are to very, very well established scientists in my field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret observed renewal patterns with the understanding that established investigators may be overrepresented among successful renewals — consider how PI track record may affect your competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tip: submit renewals anyway but diversify plans
rubrics_metrics.description: You are going to have to submit them, because why not. But thinking this will be an easy, or ever an easier, path to your next interval of funding is, in my view, statistically a mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File renewal applications when appropriate, but do not make them your sole strategy — pursue parallel applications and alternative funding to mitigate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for fair career evaluation of renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: And then go fight for why renewing a R01 should no longer be viewed as anything special in your career evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where institutional review places undue weight on renewals, engage colleagues/leadership to recalibrate hiring/promotion evaluation criteria so that sequential 'new' funding is not penalized versus renewals.
